SMTO-GML-0012 — Too many Gmail changes are waiting at once

GUID: 6f13e072-ab08-470b-af3b-7312d7ea0cc9
Slug: gmail-bulk-too-many-selections
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO keeps a short list of email previews that are waiting for approval, and that list is full, or one change tried to touch too many emails at once. Nothing was changed by this request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait about 10 minutes before asking SMTO for another preview of emails to change. Each preview stays reserved for 10 minutes, and SMTO clears old ones automatically after that.
  2. Avoid asking for many separate bulk changes in a row; finish or cancel one change before starting the next. Every new preview takes one of the limited places, even if you never approve it.
  3. If you listed a very large number of specific emails, ask SMTO to choose them by a search instead, for example "all emails from this sender before 2023". SMTO handles large searches in smaller groups for you, while a single direct list has a size limit.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows a new preview of the emails to change instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep asking for new previews in quick succession; that keeps the list full.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail bulk change was refused because 100 unexpired preview selections are already held in memory, or a direct batchModify call received fewer than 1 or more than 1,000 message IDs.

What this means

  • Direct provider batch modification has outside one through 1,000 IDs, or the local service already retains 100 unexpired preview selections. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Direct provider batch modification has outside one through 1,000 IDs, or the local service already retains 100 unexpired preview selections.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish excessive message IDs from exhausted preview slots before reducing the mutation set.

How to fix it

  • GmailService.preview_modify refuses a new selection when 100 unexpired (10-minute) selections exist in GmailService._selections; GmailRestClient.batch_modify_messages rejects batches outside 1 to 1,000 IDs. Let pending selections expire (10 minutes) or consume them via gmail.batch_modify, and send direct REST batches in chunks of at most 1,000 IDs (GmailService.modify_messages already chunks).
  • Keep direct batch IDs within the supported bound; if pending previews are full, let them settle or expire before creating another.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended request fits its actual bound and unused previews settle or expire.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
